spec_match.rationale: A decision-tooling angle on the feature: maps six real product scenarios to the coarsest workable radius and the accuracyMode each implies, generating the exact getCurrentPosition call (including the precise-mode enableHighAccuracy pairing) rather than a generic snippet.

interactive.rationale: Six toggle buttons with aria-pressed state drive the shaded log-scale band, three verdict tiles, the generated snippet and the rationale text (auto-selection at load observed live), plus a copy-to-clipboard action with a selection fallback.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises picking what you are building and seeing the coarsest radius that works, which mode to request, and what asking finer costs — the page delivers precisely those three outputs.

edge_cases.rationale: Copy-before-selecting is handled, clipboard refusal falls back to selecting the snippet with an explanation, and the case set includes the boundary where approximate genuinely stops working (transit, navigation) so the tool does not oversell the coarse mode.

conformance.rationale: Backed by the feature-level suite; on Chromium 141 the route ran 6 pass / 2 fail, the expected pre-157 split — this advisory page makes no runtime claims that suite does not cover.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): the load-time auto-selection genuinely ran (console 'selected locator: works to 1200m, mode approximate'; both screenshots show the pressed Nearest-branch button, shaded band to 1.2 km, populated tiles and generated snippet); the other five cases and the copy action are click-driven and judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires 'budget-selected' on every selection including the observed initial one and 'snippet-copied' on copy; console is clean.

design_system.rationale: All colours are variables, the pressed case-button state swaps background and colour together, the band is a translucent accent-blue non-text element, and text contrast passes AA throughout.

accessibility.rationale: Case buttons are real buttons with aria-pressed, the scale is role=img labelled by a text line that restates the band in words, verdicts are a definition list, the rationale lands in an aria-live=polite output, and the clipboard fallback keeps copy keyboard-reachable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: case buttons stack to one column, the scale band and marks fit, tiles stack, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped control on either class.

openQuestions.title: The works-to radii are editorial numbers presented as findings
openQuestions.detail: Each case's 'works to N m' threshold (20 km timezone, 12 km weather, 1.2 km branches, 800 m delivery, 120 m transit, 15 m navigation) is asserted without a source or derivation. The store-locator sibling actually demonstrates its threshold empirically; this page could either link each number to evidence (that demo, forecast-grid documentation, stop-spacing data) or label the column as a rule-of-thumb, so a reviewer cannot mistake editorial judgment for measurement.

openQuestions.title: Approximate/precise cutoff at 500 m is invisible logic
openQuestions.detail: The mode recommendation flips on works >= 500 inside select(); the 800 m delivery case gets 'approximate' and the 120 m transit case 'precise', but nothing in the UI explains where the boundary sits or why. One sentence in the note (tying the cutoff to the expected radius of Chrome's approximate fixes) would make the tool's reasoning inspectable.

summary: A genuinely useful configuration/decision angle that rounds out the feature's portfolio: pick a scenario, see the coarsest radius that still answers it, the mode to request, and the privacy cost of asking finer, with a correctly-formed call to copy. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/approximate-geolocation/precision-budget/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots showing the observed auto-selected Nearest-branch state with band, tiles and snippet rendered; clean console; feature /conformance/ route 6 pass / 2 fail as expected pre-157). Remaining questions are about epistemics rather than behaviour: the thresholds and the 500 m mode cutoff are sensible but unsourced, and should either cite evidence or admit to being rules of thumb.
